waste_flags.message: Flood irrigation on corn loses about 21 acre-ft per year compared with drip.
Sprinkler irrigation on oats loses about 0.9 acre-ft per year compared with drip.

assumptions: Mature, full-producing orchards.
Weather is regional (NASA POWER grid cell about 50 km wide).
Yield losses from weather and water only. Nutrients, pests, and disease are assumed well managed.
Reference ET0 is FAO-56 Penman-Monteith from NASA POWER daily weather.
Crop water use is ETc = Kc x ET0 with the FAO-56 single crop coefficient curve.
Effective rain: rain under 5 mm in a day is lost, and 80 percent of larger rains reach the root zone (Dastane 1974, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 25).
Irrigation refills the root zone when half of the available water is used (FAO-56 soil water balance). The root zone starts each season full.
Relative yield uses FAO-33: 1 - Ya/Ym = Ky x (1 - ETa/ETc). Each heat stress day above this location's normal count takes another 0.25 percent off, up to 10 percent.
Seasons that cross the new year are counted in the year they end.
Dormant orchards and alfalfa are not irrigated outside their growing season.
Some crop parameters are placeholders still being checked against FAO sources: almonds, corn, oats, processing_tomatoes.
Almond yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Walnut yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Alfalfa hay yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Almond production cost uses the Sacramento Valley study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
Walnut production cost uses the Sacramento Valley study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
Processing tomato production cost uses the San Joaquin Valley South study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
No production cost study for oat in any region, so it has no production cost.
Surface water price uses a typical Merced Irrigation District value. Actual district rates vary.
Block b4 (oats) has no production cost, so its revenue, cost, and profit are shown as no data.
Revenue uses the same median-normalized harvest quantity as the harvest-weight display.
Prices: each year uses that year's USDA NASS price.
Applied water is 35% surface water at $50 per acre-ft and 65% groundwater pumped from 150 ft (about $38 per acre-ft in 2016).
Farm dollar totals only add up blocks with price data (left out: b4 (oats)).
The summary's high, low, and typical years are ranked by farm profit.
Harvest weight is the selected county or statewide median yield scaled by how each year's relative yield compares with this block's median year, so a typical year shows a typical county harvest.
Frost occurred within 45 days of planting in 5 of 5 years for block b4 (oats planted in Nov).
Budget check uses farm cost from blocks with price data only, so the real total may be higher.
